# Automatic transmission fluid change

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Drain old fluid, drive briefly, then repeat drain and fill two more times. [t2001]

[Partial] Install an in-line transmission filter into the fluid line, then fill with new fluid. [t2001]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Drain the old fluid from the pan.
2. Drive the vehicle for a short distance to circulate fresh fluid through the system.
3. [Partial] Repeat the drain and fill cycle two more times, driving between each.

_Procedure reported by [t2001]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2001] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install an in-line filter into the fluid line.
2. [Partial] Fill with new fluid and run the vehicle to check for leaks.

</details>

## Parts

- In-line transmission filter: Approximately $30.00 [t2001]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use this method if you do not have access to a shop machine or want to avoid pressurizing the radiator with soft lines. [t2001]
- Perform multiple cycles rather than one large flush to gently replace fluid without causing issues in older transmissions. [t2001]
- The stock unit is described as more of a screen than a true filter. [t2001]
- An in-line filter provides peace of mind and is easy to add for long-term ownership. [t2001]
